If f (z) in S, it is known that for fixed λ, the orders of magnitude of Iλ (r, f ) and Iλ (r, f ′ ) are maximal when f (z) is the Koebe function. For the best results in this direction, see Bazilevič [69]. If f in S and |f | < M , or if f in Σ, it is almost trivial from the area principle that I1 (r, f ′ ) = o(1 − r)− 2 , as r → 1. Clunie and Pommerenke [166] have improved this to 1 1 I1 (r, f ′ ) = O(1 − r)− 2 + 300 . A function f (z) in S is said to be convex if the image of D by w = f (z) is a convex domain D in the w-plane, i.e. for any two points w1 , w2 in D, the straight line segment w1 , w2 also lies in D. A function F (z) in Σ is said to be convex if the complement of the image of |z| > 1 by F (z) is convex.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ and let $S$ denote the class of functions
$$f(z)=z+a_2z^2+a_3z^3+\cdots$$
which are holomorphic and univalent in $\mathbb{D}$. Let $\Sigma$ denote the class of functions
$$F(z)=z+b_0+\frac{b_1}{z}+\frac{b_2}{z^2}+\cdots$$
which are meromorphic and univalent in $\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|>1\}$.

For $\lambda>0$ and $0<r<1$ (respectively $r>1$ when $f\in\Sigma$), define the integral means
$$I_\lambda(r,f)=\left\{\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}|f(re^{i\theta})|^\lambda\,d\theta\right\}^{1/\lambda}.$$

Determine the exact (sharp) bounds, as functions of $r$ and $\lambda$, for
$$I_\lambda(r,f)\quad\text{and}\quad I_\lambda(r,f')$$
over all $f\in S$, and over all $f\in\Sigma$. That is, find
$$\sup_{f\in S} I_\lambda(r,f),\quad \sup_{f\in S} I_\lambda(r,f'),\quad \sup_{f\in\Sigma} I_\lambda(r,f),\quad \sup_{f\in\Sigma} I_\lambda(r,f')$$
as explicit functions of $r$ and $\lambda$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of determining the exact (sharp) bounds for integral means of univalent functions and their derivatives is closely tied to the integral means spectrum and Brennan's conjecture, both of which remain open in general. While sharp asymptotic orders are known to be attained by the Koebe function for $f\in S$ (with refinements due to Bazilevič, Clunie–Pommerenke, and others), and the integral means spectrum has been completely determined for some special subclasses (e.g., univalent rational functions), the exact bounds for all $\lambda$ and $r$ on $S$ and $\Sigma$ are not known. Recent works (e.g., 2024–2025 papers on integral means spectrum functionals on Teichmüller spaces and on Brennan's conjecture) continue to study this problem, indicating it remains open.

status_evidence.title: Complex exponential integral means spectrums of univalent functions and Brennan conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Determines integral means spectrums for special subclasses and discusses the still-open Brennan conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Sharp integral means / Brennan's conjecture remain open in general; only specific subclasses are settled.

status_evidence.title: Integral means spectrum functionals on Teichmüller spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the integral means spectrum (IMS) of conformal maps as functionals on Teichmüller spaces.
status_evidence.claim: The sharp form of the integral means spectrum for the universal class of univalent functions remains an active open problem.

status_evidence.title: On Brennan's conjecture in conformal mapping (Bertilsson)
status_evidence.snippet: Bertilsson's thesis gives best known partial bounds toward sharp integral means estimates.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial estimates toward the sharp bounds are known.
